projects.title: Credit-Eligibility Platform
projects.summary: Ingests financial statements from PDF, spreadsheets, bank files and accounting exports, then scores companies for short-term credit eligibility.
projects.description: The Intelligent Financial Assistant, a .NET 8 finance platform for short-term credit eligibility. Client companies are onboarded and approved by an admin team after review, then submit about three years of historical statements plus ongoing annual, monthly and bank statements (PDF, CSV, XLSX). ETL pipelines normalise balance sheets and income statements and compute metrics such as liquidity and debt-to-equity, while RabbitMQ workers run the processing with real-time status over SignalR. Blazor portals give admins and clients grid, pivot and chart reporting. I designed and built it end to end over more than three years: architecture, database, APIs, Blazor front ends and workers. It is in production and still evolving.
challenges: Turning fragmented PDF table output into balance sheets and income statements, including multi-page statements
Normalising many input shapes (PDF, templated spreadsheets, bank CSVs, accounting exports) into one model
Making reloads safe when files are re-uploaded or jobs are retried
Giving users live progress for long-running processing
outcomes: Heuristic PDF pipeline: weighted keyword scoring, note-page rejection and a page-stitching state machine
Common extract/transform/load contract across six ingestion paths, with raw-to-validated staging tables
Transactional bulk loading with SqlBulkCopy and temp-table MERGE upserts
Accounting-ratio engine (liquidity, solvency, coverage, turnover) on decimal arithmetic
RabbitMQ-driven workers with real-time status to the browser over SignalR
Blazor admin and client portals with Syncfusion grids, pivot tables and charts, Excel export and a step-by-step monthly upload wizard
APIs for client onboarding, admin approval and statement uploads, including re-upload of an already processed month
187 versioned database migrations managed with DbUp
projects.role: Full-stack engineer and principal engineer on the platform: architecture, database design, APIs, ETL and workers, and the Blazor front ends.

Isolating data between broker legal entities
outcomes: Worker pipeline: file load, roll-up, brokerage, validation, invoicing and sending, driven by job rows
Brokerage rules covering per-lot, per-trade, percentage and split-party rates, plus OTC trades
Invoice generation per client and currency with PDF and CSV output
Idempotent clearer-file ingestion over SFTP
Broker-entity multi-tenancy through JWT claims
OTC equity module with an 8-step deposit-form wizard that generates compliance PDFs

projects.title: Multi-Sport Data ETL Services
projects.summary: Per-sport .NET 8 ETL services that load provider feeds into SQL Server in bulk; the American football service adds a SQL outbox relay publishing events to RabbitMQ.
projects.description: A family of ETL services, one per sport, that pull schedules, box scores, projections and reference data from external providers (SportsDataIO for American football and basketball, Roanuz for football and cricket) and load them into per-sport SQL Server databases. The American football solution is the most complete: a clean-architecture layout (domain, application use cases, data access, hosted workers), raw provider payloads kept in MongoDB, and an outbox relay that publishes calculation events to the multi-tenant fantasy platform.
challenges: Loading large weekly datasets repeatedly without duplicates or partial failures
Surviving unauthorized and transient provider API failures without losing a whole run
Publishing events exactly once from several instances without distributed transactions
Reusing one pattern across four sports and two providers
outcomes: Hosted worker services calling single-purpose use cases (reference-data sync, box scores by week, player projections by week, headshot sync) on a schedule
Bulk upserts through staging tables and MERGE, with a lookback window for incremental sync and per-match transaction boundaries
Item-level fault tolerance: a failing match or call is logged and skipped while the rest of the run continues
Outbox written in the same transaction as the game data; a hosted publisher claims batches with READPAST/UPDLOCK, retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and resets stuck locks
Typed shared event contracts consumed through EasyNetQ AutoSubscriber by the fantasy platform
Relational schema for competitions, tournaments, timeframes, teams, players, schedules, scores, quarters and scoring plays, with versioned migrations
Unit and integration-style data-access and API-client tests, and pipelines publishing the worker deployables
Player image pipeline that validates, resizes and publishes photos to blob storage
projects.role: Lead backend engineer and solution architect on the American football platform (schema, clean-architecture refactor, use cases, outbox, testing, CI/CD); built the football, cricket and basketball ETL services on the same patterns.

projects.title: Fantasy Sports Platform (in progress)
projects.summary: Multi-tenant fantasy sports back end: daily contest creation, and leaderboard workers that consume match events idempotently. American football is implemented; the platform did not reach full release.
projects.description: A white-label fantasy sports platform on .NET 8 and SQL Server. A contest-creation worker creates American football tournaments daily. A leaderboard worker consumes match events from the sports data services over RabbitMQ, applies them with a per-match checkpoint, updates points in one transaction, and polls for matches whose events were missed. Each white-label operator has its own database, resolved per request. The leaderboard side was only partly finished: American football is implemented end to end, other sports are stubbed, and prize calculation is a placeholder.
challenges: Keeping leaderboards correct when events arrive twice, late or not at all
Isolating each white-label operator's data while sharing one API
Structuring the contest and leaderboard logic so more sports can be added
outcomes: Daily scheduled worker that creates American football tournaments, with run-now override and retry policy
Event consumer plus checkpoint on the source-updated timestamp, so duplicate or older events are skipped
Polling hosted service that finds matches with pending updates and reprocesses them when events were missed
One database transaction per match: player points, team totals and tournament-match final state are updated together
Database-per-operator tenancy resolved per request from the broker context and bound to the caller through a JWT claim
Per-sport processing entry points in place (football, cricket, basketball, baseball, hockey) pending implementation
Unit and integration-style data-access tests for contest, team and settings commands and queries
projects.role: Lead backend architect and principal .NET engineer: designed the tenancy model and event-driven leaderboard flow, built the APIs, workers and data-access layer.

projects.title: Clean Architecture Reference Platform
projects.summary: A .NET 8 reference implementation with compiler-enforced layer boundaries, proposed to engineering leadership for a multi-tenant SaaS product.
projects.description: While maintaining APIs for an EHS SaaS platform, I designed a working reference architecture to show how a legacy monolith could move to a modular one. It covers authentication, per-request tenant resolution, a reusable list-view query pipeline and architecture tests that fail the build on layer violations, and I presented it with an executive brief and developer guide.
challenges: Proving a strict architecture is practical inside an existing legacy codebase
Keeping legacy password and token formats working with new endpoints
Building one safe, reusable pipeline for filtered, sorted, paged lists
Resolving each request's tenant database without leaking credentials
outcomes: Eight architecture tests enforcing layer dependencies in CI
List-view pipeline with 16 filter operators, global and per-field search and row-level authorization
Per-request tenant connection resolution with encrypted credentials
Six sign-in paths: password, one-time code, session token, impersonation and reset
Hybrid data access: EF Core for writes with audit snapshots, Dapper for reads
projects.role: Designed and built the reference platform and wrote the executive brief and developer guide.

projects.title: Textile ERP (Inventory & Setup Framework)
projects.summary: An internal ERP for a textile unit (2018 to 2021): I worked on the Inventory module and other modules, wrote a metadata-driven setup framework, and sped up a daily management report. Not all modules were completed.
projects.description: An ASP.NET MVC and Web API system for a textile unit within a group of several garments units, replacing paper and spreadsheet tracking. The codebase has 548 entities and 159 controllers across yarn procurement, inventory, knitting, R&D and lab testing, costing and booking analysis. Not every module was completed during my time. I worked on the Inventory module (yarn receive, QC, issue, return, transfer and requisition) and several other modules, wrote the Common Interface framework for setup pages, optimised a daily management report, and gathered requirements directly from factory teams.
challenges: Keeping stock transactions (receive, QC, issue, return, transfer) consistent across a long production chain
A management report that took about 10 minutes every morning
Avoiding a new controller, view and script for every setup table
outcomes: Inventory module (among other modules): yarn receive, receive QC, issue, issue return, transfer and requisition screens backed by the ERP's repository and specification layers
Common Interface: a metadata-driven setup-page framework (screen, fields, grids, lookups and SQL stored as configuration rows, served by one generic API and view), so new setup pages need no new code
Daily management report cut from about 10 minutes to 1 to 2 minutes through SQL rewrites, indexing and an API
projects.role: Senior engineer: worked on the Inventory module and other modules, wrote Common Interface, and informally mentored and led a small team without a formal title.
